relationships.description: The access condition is one comparison term inside a policy rule's condition expression, existing only as part of that rule and contributing its true/false result to the rule's permit or deny decision.
relationships.evidence: The policy definition file (e.g. OPA/Rego, XACML or a YAML policy) nests the attribute comparison inside the rule's condition block, so deleting the rule removes the comparison with it.

relationships.description: The access condition narrows when a granted permission actually applies, so a holder of the permission may perform the action on the resource only if the runtime attribute comparison is true.
relationships.evidence: The authorization configuration attaches the condition to the permission grant (e.g. an IAM policy 'Condition' block or a @PreAuthorize expression combining hasPermission with an attribute check), and requests failing the comparison are denied despite the role holding the permission.

relationships.description: The access condition decides at runtime whether the field access control's masking, redaction or tokenization is applied to a field, such as unmasking a value only when the subject's clearance claim meets a threshold.
relationships.evidence: The field-masking configuration or serializer code checks the condition's attribute comparison before applying or skipping the mask on that named field.

relationships.description: The access condition names a property of the secure resource, such as owner, classification or tenant, as the attribute or comparison value it tests, without depending on the resource's functionality.
relationships.evidence: The condition's attribute path points into the resource context (e.g. 'resource.ownerId == subject.sub' or 'resource.classification'), and the referenced property is declared on that protected resource's schema.

relationships.description: The access condition delegates checking an attribute value's format, range or allowed-value set to a validation rule, using the rule's verdict as part of the comparison before it returns its access result.
relationships.evidence: The condition's implementation or policy expression invokes the named validation check (e.g. a shared regex or allowed-list function) on the request attribute, and an invalid value causes the condition to evaluate false with its denial message.

notes: composes direction looks inverted: the catalog says whole composes part, yet here the part (AccessCondition) composes the whole (PolicyRule); 'composed-of' or swapping the direction fits better. Using ValidationRule muddles concerns, since validation accepts values and conditions make access decisions. Governs over FieldAccessControl partly overlaps with constrains.
